abstract: Saccharomyces boulardii is a widely used probiotic yeast, yet its functional distinction from closely related Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains and the consistency of traits across commercial isolates remain unclear. Here, we performed integrated genomic, physiological, metabolic, and host-cell analyses of five S. boulardii isolates and three distinct S. cerevisiae strains. Despite high genomic similarity, S. boulardii exhibited conserved lineage-specific features, including a chromosomal inversion, reduced CAZyme copy numbers, and consistent sequence variation in metabolic pathways. Functionally, S. boulardii isolates showed enhanced acid tolerance, elevated acetate and succinate production, and reproducible immunomodulatory activity, including NF-κB suppression and reduced IL-8 and TNF-α secretion. All isolates consistently activated the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), unlike other S. cerevisiae strains, which instead displayed faster growth and greater bile tolerance. Overall, probiotic-relevant phenotypes were conserved across S. boulardii, defining it as a functionally coherent probiotic lineage.
